source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1955, p. 4 ("Contests in Londonderry, Limavady and Coleraine: three Limavady R.D.C. seats to be contested; full list of nominations"); Derry Journal, 18 May 1955, p. 2 ("Limavady Rural Council: four seats will be contested; full list of nominations"); Londonderry Standard, 20 May 1955, p. 5 ("Limavady Rural battle: Drumraighland withdrawal; H. Marshall returned unopposed")
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed after a withdrawal: 'Eight candidates were nominated for four seats on Tuesday, but yesterday there was a withdrawal. Edward McGowan, the Nationalist member of Drumraighland, stood down in favour of the Unionist nominee, Robert J. Townley' (Londonderry Sentinel 19 May 1955 p4, image read; also Londonderry Standard 20 May 1955 p5).

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled Thursday 2 June 1955. Three contests; the report says there were three, although an earlier nominations report had expected four (Derry Journal, 3 June 1955, p. 1). Eleven unopposed members added (Aghanloo to Gelvin) from the full nominations list (Derry Journal, 18 May 1955, p. 2; Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1955, p. 4), whose printed text stops at Gelvin; Glenshane, Keady, Killywool, Lislane, Myroe, Owenreagh, Scriggan, Straw and The Highlands are not yet found (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
